title: Japan Ku-area of Tokyo CPI (December 2026, preliminary) + 2026 Tokyo yearly average
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), re-fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table by this session, independently of the fetch that seeded japan-cpi-2027-01-22. Against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks', the row parses exactly as ['November', 'December 18', 'December', 'December 25', '2026 yearly average of Ku-area of Tokyo'] — i.e. the Tokyo December preliminary CPI and the 2026 Tokyo yearly average both release on 2026-12-25. Filed estimate on three counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page has not been refreshed since 2026-01-23, so its far-forward rows are the movable half. Release time is not read off this page and is not asserted here.
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2027-01-22 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and tracked for one reason: it is the 28-day pre-announcement of that event's own headline. The Ku-area-of-Tokyo flash is a subsample of the national basket and leads the national print by construction — this lane measured how well. Using the Statistics Bureau's own 2025-base monthly index files (e-Stat stat-search/file-download?statInfId=000040491314 for Japan and 000040491317 for Tokyo, fileKind=4, parsed locally out of the OOXML: 679 national observations 1970-01 to 2026-07 and 680 Tokyo 1970-01 to 2026-08), the Tokyo-minus-national year-on-year gap for the same month over 103 months (2018-01 to 2026-07) on the BoJ's core measure (all items less fresh food) has mean -0.073pp, MEAN ABSOLUTE 0.201pp, sd 0.259, worst month 0.85pp, and lands within +/-0.3pp in 78% of months and +/-0.5pp in 92%. So by this date roughly four readers in five already know the national December print (releasing 2027-01-22) to within a rounding step. Impact is LOW: symbols is empty, no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI, and this entry's value is calibration and attribution rather than a trade. Two further dated facts from the same primary table, recorded here so the next session does not re-fetch them: the Tokyo January-2027 flash follows on 2027-01-29, and every one of the 30 release dates in the Bureau's table falls on a Tuesday or a Friday. Registered against FT-japan-cpi-2027-01-22-1, which scores the Tokyo-to-national gap at a +/-0.3pp threshold on 2027-01-23. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25.md), which qualifies the framing above on three counts measured from the same primaries. FIRST, the lead is marginal against a free alternative the discovery sweep never raced it against: over the identical 103 months the Tokyo flash predicts national core y/y with 0.201pp mean absolute error, but simply reusing last month's national print — published seven days earlier on 2026-12-18 — gets 0.231pp and is BETTER at the +/-0.5pp bar (94% vs 92%); a 50/50 blend beats both at 0.175pp (84%/98%). So the edge over doing nothing is about 0.03pp, and 'roughly four readers in five already know the national print' credits this release with information that was mostly public a week earlier. SECOND, 2026-12-25 is a Friday and Christmas Day: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (fetched direct 2026-09-05, HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes) lists Christmas Day 2026 as 'Friday, December 25' — a full NYSE closure — with a 1:00 p.m. ET early close the day before, while JPX's own 2026 holiday list (21 dates, Jan 1 through Dec 31) does not include Dec 25, so Tokyo trades normally. Checked mechanically against every event file, this is the ONLY tracked event dated on an NYSE holiday. That makes attribution WORSE, not better: there is no US tape on the print's own date, the first US session is Monday 2026-12-28 which carries its own print, and the channel-kill test is therefore scoped to 2026-12-24. THIRD, this release carries one new number rather than two — its second headline, the 2026 Tokyo yearly average, is 11/12 fixed by the Tokyo November flash on 2026-11-27 (proposed as japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-11-27 in the same PR) and its twelfth month arrives in this same release; a +/-1.0pp December surprise moves it +/-0.084pp against a one-decimal publication. Projected at +1.6% to +1.9% versus a computed +2.85% for 2025. Also recorded for the 2027 sessions: Tokyo's reduced-rate basket weight is 19.50% (Food 2682 - Alcoholic 100 - Meals outside the home 632) against 21.35% nationally, so from the 2027-04-01 food consumption-tax cut the Tokyo flash under-reads the national drag by 0.12pp in a known direction — more than half its entire historical mean absolute error. Three forward tests registered in docs/research/forward-tests/japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25.md, scored 2026-12-26, 2027-01-23 and 2026-12-26.
